# Dictionary

**Generated from `docs/dictionary.yml` by `npm run gen:dictionary` — do not edit this file.**

One name per concept. A term listed under **not** fails the build, naming its replacement.
Vocabulary already in the docs when the gate shipped is grandfathered and does not have to
be registered — but registering it is always welcome, and registering one is how its
alternates start being caught.

16 terms.

| Term | Says | Not |
|---|---|---|
| **API** | the routes a program calls to get data, as opposed to the pages a person reads. Here, the server's /api routes the phone and the map call | — |
| **DDL** | data definition language: the SQL that creates and alters tables, as opposed to the SQL that reads and writes rows | — |
| **GEOS** | the geometry library PostGIS calls to cut, join and compare shapes; its version decides some results | — |
| **GPS** | the satellite positioning a phone or watch records a ride with | — |
| **GPX** | GPS Exchange Format: an open XML standard for recorded points and lines. Gaia exports tracks in it | — |
| **HTML** | the markup a web page is written in | — |
| **HTMX** | a small JavaScript library that lets a plain HTML page swap in a fragment the server sends, instead of a client app rendering it | — |
| **HTTP** | how the app and the phone ask a server for a page or data; plain, it is not encrypted unless something underneath is | — |
| **JSON** | the text format the API answers in. The Rust server must answer with the same JSON the TypeScript one does | — |
| **OSM** | OpenStreetMap, the open map the streets are loaded from | — |
| **SQL** | the language the database is queried in. The coverage SQL is copied from the TypeScript repo verbatim | — |
| **SRID** | the number naming a geometry's coordinate system. Every geometry here is 4326, plain longitude and latitude | — |
| **URL** | the address of a page or an API route | — |
| **UTC** | the world clock time with no time zone; timestamps are stored in it and shown in Cleveland time | — |
| **VPS** | a rented virtual server; mill-dev, the dev machine, is one | — |
| **XML** | a text format of nested tags, like HTML but for data | — |
